extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys/practitioners registered to practice before the USPTO; OED staff; attorneys facing USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, rules, procedures, and remedial/sanctioning criteria applied by the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline when evaluating and disciplining registered patent (and other) practitioners for professional misconduct (including fee/payment-related misconduct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Disciplinary Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners registered to practice before the USPTO are subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration status and jurisdictional qualification (e.g., registration number, state admission) determine that a practitioner is bound by the USPTO's disciplinary rules. The Final Order repeatedly cites the practitioner's registration number and that he is subject to the Disciplinary Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional basis for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutes and regulations provide the legal authority for OED investigations, settlement agreements, issuance of Final Orders, and imposition of sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment requirement (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees and charges payable to the USPTO are required to be paid in advance; i.e., at the time of requesting any action for which a fee or charge is payable (37 C.F.R. § 1.22).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment methods include check, cashier's check, money order, credit card (37 C.F.R. § 1.23), electronic funds transfer or authorization to charge a USPTO deposit account if established (37 C.F.R. § 1.25). Failure to pay required fees can have substantive consequences (see issue fee timing and abandonment rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date and payment exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. § 1.53, applications for patent may be assigned a filing date without payment of the basic filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrow exception to the general advance-payment rule is statutory/regulatory and may be relevant to counseling clients about formal filing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue fee timing under 35 U.S.C. § 151
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is allowed, a written notice of allowance specifies the issue fee (or portion) which must be paid within three months; if not timely paid the application is regarded as abandoned; remaining balances must be paid within three months of notice or the patent shall lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must advise clients and ensure timely payment of issue fees to avoid abandonment or lapse of patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice is proscribed by 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order finds that submitting checks that are returned for insufficient funds can constitute such prejudicial conduct. This standard is used to evaluate practitioner behavior that undermines USPTO processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct reflecting adversely on practitioner's fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that reflects adversely on a practitioner's fitness to practice is proscribed by 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial mismanagement (e.g., issuing checks on insufficient funds) can be found to reflect adversely on fitness to practice and supports disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct example: issuing checks returned for insufficient funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Signing and submitting checks to the USPTO that are returned for insufficient funds (here, 18 checks totaling $34,421.00) is actionable misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practitioner's issuance of returned checks was the factual basis for violations of §§ 10.23(b)(5) and (b)(6). OED treats returned checks for payment of USPTO fees as serious professional failings because fees must be timely paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remediation actions that mitigate discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedial steps taken by a practitioner (e.g., depositing client advances in an IOLTA account, restricting disbursement procedures, assigning responsibility to a single individual, increasing bookkeeping oversight, completing ethics courses) are relevant mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists specific remedial measures taken by the respondent: (i) deposit all client advances in an Interest on Lawyers Trust Account (IOLTA), (ii) disburse USPTO fees only from client advances in the IOLTA, (iii) assign a single person responsibility for checks/disbursements, and (iv) increase bookkeeper hours; respondent also completed ethics training (4-hour and 3-hour CBA courses). Such measures reduce the risk of recurrence and are weighed in discipline determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making good on returned payments and client notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners should make good on returned checks and inform affected clients; doing so is a mitigating factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent repaid the returned checks and informed clients, and the Final Order notes no apparent client harm—these facts contributed to mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors considered (general list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors mitigating discipline include lack of prior disciplinary history, acceptance of responsibility, cooperation with investigation, remedial efforts, and absence of client harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites that respondent had no prior discipline in 22 years, cooperated, accepted responsibility, undertook remedial measures, and no clients appear harmed; such factors reduced the discipline to a stayed suspension plus probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning options and structure (suspension, stay, probation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may impose suspensions, stays of suspension, probationary periods, and other conditions; here, a 24‑month suspension was imposed but stayed, and the respondent was placed on 24 months' probation during which he may practice unless the stay is lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly conditions the stay on compliance during probation; if the stay is not lifted by the end of probation, the suspension need not be served. 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60 apply if suspension is actually imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation enforcement procedure (Order to Show Cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED believes the respondent failed to comply during probation, OED shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to respondent's last address of record, and grant 15 days to respond; if still unsatisfied, OED forwards materials to the USPTO Director requesting lifting of the stay and imposition of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This delineates the stepwise enforcement process: (1) OED issues Order to Show Cause; (2) 15 days to respond; (3) after consideration, OED may deliver the OSC, the response, and supporting evidence to the Director and request lifting the stay and suspension up to 24 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if stay is lifted (immediate suspension mechanics)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the stay is lifted, the respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; OED shall disseminate information under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; USPTO will dissociate the respondent's name from customer numbers and PKI certificates; the respondent may not use or obtain USPTO customer numbers or PKI certificates until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are operational consequences intended to effectuate the suspension: dissociation from electronic credentials and public notice; reinstatement is required before re-obtaining credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish Final Orders in the OED Reading Room and publish Notices of Stayed Suspension in the Official Gazette; pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the Director must notify state disciplinary agencies, courts where the respondent is admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary outcomes are publicly posted and formally notified to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts as required by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of the disciplinary proceeding in future complaints or proceedings either as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by or on respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior settled disciplinary record is not sealed off from future consideration; the Office may use it to increase discipline or rebut claims in later matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of review of Director's lifting-of-stay decision
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director lifts the stay and the respondent seeks review of that decision, such review does not postpone or hold in abeyance the immediate suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative review does not stay the effect of an immediate suspension once the Director lifts the stayed suspension.
